title: Mujaddara
subtitle: Lebanese lentils and rice with crispy caramelised onions
excerpt: Green lentils and long-grain rice cooked together with warm spices, then topped with deeply caramelised, almost crispy onions. One of Lebanon's great comfort dishes and entirely plant-based.
sourceNotes: Mujaddara is one of the oldest documented dishes in the world. It appears in a 13th-century Arabic cookbook and has been a staple across the Levant for centuries. The name comes from the Arabic word for pockmarked, referring to the lentils dotted through the rice.

recipe.batchNotes: Good for batch cooking. Reheat with a splash of water.

content.text: The onions are the whole point of this dish. Take your time with them. They should be very dark and almost crispy at the edges, not just softened. This takes a full 30 minutes over a medium heat.
Start the onions first. Heat 4 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat.
Add all the onion. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until very dark and jammy.
Meanwhile, cook the lentils in a large saucepan with plenty of water for 15 minutes. They should be just tender but not falling apart. Drain.
Return the lentils to the pan. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil and all the ground spices. Stir well.
Add the rinsed rice and 500ml of water. Season with salt.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to the lowest heat. Put the lid on.
Cook for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave to steam with the lid on for 5 more minutes.
Fluff the rice and lentils with a fork. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Pile the caramelised onions on top to serve.

items.cause: Too much water was added or the heat was too high.
items.fix: Use exactly 500ml of water and keep the heat very low once the lid goes on.

items.symptom: Onions softened but never crisped up.
items.cause: The pan was too crowded or the heat too low.
items.fix: Use a wide pan and cook on medium heat for the full 30 minutes.
